For q-102693, integrating acceleration gives v(t)=3t+4t²−t³−1, so speed at t=2 is 13 m/s. For q-102742, v(t)=(2/5)t^(5/2), giving 2/5 m/s. For q-81710, v(t)=3−2cos(2t), giving 5 ft/s at π/2. Parametric arc length is the integral of sqrt(x′²+y′²): q-15174 has squared speed 18t⁴+8t², whose square root is t sqrt(18t²+8) on [0,1]; q-85724 has squared speed 9t⁴+4t²−4t+1; q-15182 has squared speed 9sin²(3t)+9cos²(t); q-123030 has squared speed 25sin²(5t)+36cos²(t). For q-10256, speed is 3sin(t)cos(t) on [0,π/2], integrating to 3/2. For q-47918, D is the highest included point over the domain. For q-103437, x=−1 is a smooth local minimum, so the derivative is zero and the point is critical; statements I and II hold, while III does not. For q-74640, multiplying by the conjugate gives (5+10i)/5=1+2i. For q-8506, r=17 and the third-quadrant angle π+arctan(15/8) rounds to 4.22 radians. For q-40756, the positive y-axis gives (12,π/2). For q-49136, differentiating 2arcsec(x)−3sin(x)+C gives the stated derivative on |x|>1, using the standard arcsec branch. For q-71768, termwise integration gives x⁵+7arctan(x)+C. For q-50136, isolating and integrating y′=−4e^(2x)−2x gives y=−2e^(2x)−x²+C.
